Thanks for the flag, Rishi. Good summary. Quick notes and suggested plan of attack: 

- Scope: extending retention to 365 days will change the evidence surface (longer storage windows, retention policies). Operationally we support this on Hosted via our Log-Archive feature (adds cold-object storage and redirection of audit events); it’s typically an add-on rather than a core change to SOC 2 scope. We should confirm whether Brightline wants logs retained off-host (encrypted S3) vs within our hot cluster.

- Compliance approach: we can map existing 2025 SOC 2 controls to the questionnaire. For controls that depend on retention window, we’ll add a short rider describing retention policy and where logs are stored. This usually suffices for re-attestation; external auditor may ask for sample exports showing 365-day retention — we can produce those.

- Timeline (conservative): 1) Evidence mapping (5 business days) — Rishi to coordinate with customer and Trust; 2) Evidence extraction / storage configuration (7 business days) — Operations; 3) Customer review & auditor prep (5 business days). Plan ~3 calendar weeks if Ops prioritized.

- Deployment/cost: If Brightline increases reserved capacity to 15 on Dedicated, Ops will need 2–3 weeks lead for capacity planning. If they remain Hosted and just increase commit, we can usually accommodate within 5–7 days for account config, but retention add-on requires storage provisioning and a small monthly fee. I’ll ask Finance for a templated amendment with tiered pricing (retention + per-GB pricing).

Action items:
1) Rishi: confirm whether Brightline prefers Hosted+add-on or Dedicated reserved pool (reply to Nina).
2) Jonas: Ops contact — can you confirm ballpark lead time and whether any migration window will be needed to backfill last 12 months of logs?
3) Marissa: I’ll draft a short attestation rider and example evidence list (system configs, access reviews, audit exports, incident logs, backup policies).

I’m cc’ing the Trust/Operations leads in a follow-up. Keep me posted.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Trust, Redwood Inference

Hi Nina — thanks for the questionnaire and the sample. Quick answers and proposed next steps: 

1) Hosted + Log-Archive add-on is likely the quickest path. It allows us to retain audit events for 365 days in encrypted cold storage with export capability for auditor requests. It will add a monthly retention fee (I’ll send a draft amendment and pricing snapshot).

2) We can map our existing SOC 2 artifacts to your questionnaire. Marissa is drafting the attestation rider and will include an explicit section on retention/storage location.

3) Capacity: moving committed units from 5 -> 15 can be done under Hosted as a billing/commit change (no data migration). If you want Dedicated reserved nodes instead, Ops (Jonas) notes a 2–3 week lead time for capacity provisioning. Please confirm which you prefer.

Proposed timeline if Hosted + add-on:
- Evidence map and attachables: by 2026-12-06 (Rishi + Marissa)
- Retention config + backfill plan: by 2026-12-13 (Operations)
- Customer review & finalize amendment: by 2026-12-20
\If that works I’ll open a HubSpot task and share the amendment + price sheet.

Next step: Nina, can you confirm whether Brightline wants Hosted with the retention add-on or Dedicated capacity? Also confirm whether you need us to backfill logs to reach a full 12 months (that affects the timeline/cost).
